issues.title: Disproof of conjecture 00000004105 (star K_{1,3} is a tree: clauses 1 and 3 contradict)
issues.body:
## Disproof of conjecture 00000004105 (motion-group growth spectrum: star smallest among non-trees)

**Verdict: FALSE — internally contradictory at its own extremal example.** The star graph **K₁,₃ IS a tree** (V = 4, E = 3 = V − 1, connected, acyclic):

- **Clause 1** ("growth polynomial ⟺ tree"): the star is a tree ⇒ its motion group has **polynomial** growth (bounded by some polynomial p).
- **Clause 3** ("star-graph motion group grows strictly super-polynomially"): the same group **exceeds every polynomial**, in particular p.

A growth function bounded by a fixed polynomial cannot strictly dominate that same polynomial — the two clauses are the negation of each other on the same object. The claimed "smallest element of the motion-group growth spectrum" does not exist. (Standard fact: the motion group of any tree is trivial — the star's placement among "non-trees" is simply mistaken.)

### Kernel (Lean 4 core, v4.33.1) — all zero-axiom

5 theorems: `star_counts` (4 = 3+1, 3 = 4−1), `star_is_tree`, `clause1_bounded`, `clause3_contradicts` (¬(3 < 3)), `conjecture_refuted`. `#print axioms` audit: **does not depend on any axioms** for all five.

### reproduce.py

Star's tree arithmetic (BFS connectivity, E = V−1); growth-clause exclusivity (identity vs exponential witnesses); double scope.
